description: Add security headers, custom 404 page, prefers-reduced-motion support, and metadata template to improve the site's security posture, accessibility, and SEO.
steps: 1. Add security headers to next.config.ts: X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, X-XSS-Protection, Referrer-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, Permissions-Policy. Use the Next.js 16 headers() config in nextConfig.

2. Create app/not-found.tsx as a custom 404 page. It should be a server component that exports metadata. Include a simple, styled 'page not found' message with a link back to home. Follow the semantic HTML and Tailwind patterns used in existing pages.

3. Add prefers-reduced-motion support in app/globals.css using @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) to disable animations and transitions for users who have requested reduced motion. This is required by the PRD (respecting prefers-reduced-motion).
4. Add a metadata template in app/layout.tsx using the metadataBase and title.template pattern from Next.js so child pages can use title.default and get 'Page Name | Kiro Hub' format automatically.
5. Create app/error.tsx as a client component error boundary. It should display a user-friendly error message with a 'Try again' button that calls reset(). Follow the existing design patterns.
6. Verify the build succeeds with npm run build and npm run lint.
acceptance_criteria: npm run build completes successfully with all pages compiling
npm run lint passes with no errors
app/not-found.tsx exists and renders a custom 404 page
app/error.tsx exists and provides a client-side error boundary
app/layout.tsx uses metadata title template pattern
findings: Next.js 16 uses unstable_retry instead of reset() for error boundaries. The not-found.tsx at app root handles all unmatched URLs globally. Build and lint both pass cleanly.
